justification: Contribution is a Watchdog execution-monitoring layer plus post-grasp semantic verification feeding a bounded finalize/retry/escalate policy; validated on a lab manipulator over induced-failure scenarios, not in deployment.

MASTER's claim is the hierarchy of agent arrangements compared as peer review, triage-ranking and triage-forms against a single-agent baseline; lab simulation study on two chemical applications, no practice deployment.

Retrospex's mechanism is an offline retrospection process that trains an RL critic on the agent's own past trajectories to rescore actions; evaluated as a prototype on ScienceWorld, ALFWorld and Webshop in the lab.

BALAR is an outer-loop algorithm that decides the next clarifying question by maximising expected mutual information over a belief state; lab evaluation on AR-Bench-DC, AR-Bench-SP and iCraft-MD benchmarks.

The paper contributes a measurement study of loop behaviour (energy, duration, tokens, memory) across four agentic frameworks rather than a loop mechanism; a controlled lab evaluation on fixed hardware, 150 runs per configuration.

The contribution is an explicit affective state kept external to the model and carried across turns by update rules; a lab study over a fixed 25-turn protocol comparing stateless, first- and second-order dynamics.

The paper studies emergent collaboration and Theory-of-Mind inference among LLM agents in a cooperative text game, then adds explicit belief states; lab comparison against MARL and planning baselines, no real setting.

IAL-Scan is a diagnostic instrument that names a failure class and statically detects unbounded feedback paths, not a mechanism that bounds the loop; evaluated on a corpus of 6,549 repositories with manual confirmation.

DREAMS's contribution is a multi-tier safety guard that rejects fabricated or unsourced values at tool-call time and audits provenance at report time; lab results on the Sol27LC benchmark and the CO/Pt(111) puzzle.

AGENTSAFE proposes safeguards, dynamic authorization and escalation of high-impact actions to human oversight as gates on agentic loops; the framework is argued and mapped to taxonomies with no reported evaluation.

Agent-SAMA models app execution as a finite state machine whose states and transitions guide planning, verification and error recovery, i.e. what the loop does next; lab benchmark study on Mobile-Eval-E, SPA-Bench, AndroidWorld.

The paper theorises recursive loops of perception, evaluation, goal-updating and action, formalised as a goal-maintenance equation that determines what the system pursues next; it is a conceptual theory of agency, no method.

MAgICoRe's object is the refinement that follows a judgement: Solver-Reviewer-Refiner rounds with reward-model-localised feedback and re-evaluation; lab results across five math datasets with Llama-3-8B and GPT-3.5.

AgentQuest is a measurement instrument, a modular benchmark framework plus two progress metrics for tracking agent behaviour; the prototype is exercised on two lab use cases showing measured performance increases.

GENIUS's headline is the automated error-handling loop that repairs failing inputs after validation diagnostics, recovering 76.3% of initial failures; lab evaluation over 295 benchmark prompts, not in production use.

The contribution is an empirical characterisation of loop structure, reliability mechanisms and autonomy levels rather than a mechanism; it studies 6,000+ workflows built by real users on a deployed automation platform.

The paper's claim is about the arrangement itself, an orchestrator with restricted-communication sub-agents, and finds orchestrator capacity drives performance; controlled lab comparisons on tool-intensive benchmarks.

The thesis contributes a systematic empirical evaluation across one-shot, iterative-feedback, two-agent and tool-calling architectures, an instrument rather than a mechanism; lab runs on VerilogEval-Human and CVDP.

The contribution is a longitudinal measurement methodology isolating harness quality across 35 releases, not a loop mechanism; the model is held constant and releases varied over 50 SWE-bench Verified tasks in the lab.

SAL is a control plane that validates emitted intents against true system state and policy before execution, giving policy-bounded release; a lab prototype blocks 93% of unsafe intents on the authors' own benchmark.

The contribution is a stopping rule replacing a fixed iteration cap, cutting operational tokens 38% at parity quality; a paired lab protocol replays every stopping policy over identical HotpotQA trajectories.

The contribution is machine-checked detectors that decide whether a shared-state read-generate-write may commit, proved sound and complete; formal verification plus lab runtime runs, reproducing bugs in existing systems.

Execution lineage replaces the loop's implicit state with a DAG of artifact-producing computations whose dependencies fix what recomputes on replay; two controlled lab memo-update tasks against loop-centric baselines.

The paper contributes a live evaluation setting and trace analysis measuring planning versus execution contributions across providers; a replicated 32-game championship under frozen rules, a lab study not a deployment.

The object is what happens after validation rejects a candidate: which feedback fields make the rewrite succeed, with admissible alternatives carrying the gain; 50 paired TextWorld games under a four-call cap in the lab.
